newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Pharmacia & Upjohn says chief executive Zabriskie resigns.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia & Upjohn says chief executive Zabriskie resigns.

text.p: Swedish-American drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn said on Monday its chief executive John Zabriskie had resigned with immediate effect to return to the U.S. to pursue personal interests.
It said board chairman Jan Ekberg would resign from that position and become acting chief executive until a successor was found.
P&U said it maintained its belief in the merger between the two companies which took place in 1995.
A board committee had been set up to look for a replacement for Zabriskie, but in the meantime Ekberg, who was the managing director for Pharmacia before its merger with Upjohn, would take his place.
Richard Brown, managing director of Cable & Wireless, would be acting board head in the interim period.
"The board would like to emphasise its continued belief in the merger between Pharmacia & Upjohn and the long term strength of the company," P&U said in a statement.
Pharmacia & Upjohn shares fell on Monday after the company said Zabriskie had resigned.
At 1255 GMT the share was10 crowns lower at 274 crowns.
"I think people are a little nervous, waiting to find out what this means," said one London-based drugs sector analyst.
"There were two profit warnings last year so it could be related to that or it could mean there is more bad news to come. The stock has been marked down on the latter."
